You could really mess a Christian's head up: pop his head like a grape. We know the Bible and you don't. Shut up, listen, and learn.
precepts.point: Having predestinated us: there it go again, before the foundation of the world. Unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself. In whom we, the saints, have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Ephesians 1:4 says “he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world”. That is predestination: he chose us before the earth was made. Who is the us that was chosen? David’s psalm says it: “O ye seed of Israel his servant, ye children of Jacob, his chosen ones.”

We are the chosen ones: the seed of Israel, the children of Jacob. There are many precepts on that; Isaiah 44:1 can be used too. With these you could really mess a Christian’s head up, pop his head like a grape. We know the Bible and you don’t. Shut up, listen, and learn.

So when Paul says “Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself”, the ones predestinated and chosen are the same chosen ones of the Old Testament, the children of Jacob.

precepts.text: Be mindful always of His covenant, confirmed to Jacob for a law; the covenant carries terms.
precepts.point: It still has to be done. A covenant is a contract with terms; the covenant was confirmed to Jacob for a law, and circumcision is one of the laws within the covenant.

note.label: Genesis 17: The Covenant Sealed in the Flesh

precepts.why:
A covenant is a contract with terms. “Be ye mindful always of his covenant; the word which he commanded to a thousand generations; Even of the covenant which he made with Abraham, and of his oath unto Isaac; And hath confirmed the same to Jacob for a law, and to Israel for an everlasting covenant.”

The covenant made with Abraham was confirmed to Jacob for a law. Laws are the terms of the covenant, and circumcision is one of the laws within it: “This is my covenant, which ye shall keep.” It was commanded to a thousand generations and it is an everlasting covenant in the flesh, so it still has to be done.

precepts.text: The shorter account records the same gifts of bread, flesh, and wine to all the people.
precepts.point: David blessed the people in the name of the Most High and dealt to every man and woman a loaf of bread, a piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 16: The Song Delivered into the Hand of Asaph

precepts.why:
The shorter account in Samuel records the same gifts: “he dealt among all the people, even among the whole multitude of Israel, as well to the women as men, to every one a cake of bread, and a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine. So all the people departed every one to his house.”

Chronicles says it the same way: when the ark was set in the midst of the tent and the burnt offerings and peace offerings were made, David “blessed the people in the name of the Lord. And he dealt to every one of Israel, both man and woman, to every one a loaf of bread, and a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine.”

precepts.text: The same everlasting covenant to a thousand generations, made with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
precepts.point: The covenant was made with Abraham, sworn to Isaac, and confirmed to Jacob as an everlasting covenant, giving Israel the land of Canaan as their inheritance.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 16: The Song Delivered into the Hand of Asaph

precepts.why:
“He hath remembered his covenant for ever, the word which he commanded to a thousand generations. Which covenant he made with Abraham, and his oath unto Isaac; And confirmed the same unto Jacob for a law, and to Israel for an everlasting covenant”. It is the same song and the same everlasting covenant.

The Most High is mindful always of his covenant, and a thousand generations is to say forever. It was made with Abraham, sworn to Isaac and confirmed to Jacob as an everlasting covenant, “Saying, Unto thee will I give the land of Canaan, the lot of your inheritance”.

precepts.text: The Most High makes of Abraham a great nation, and in him all families of the earth are blessed.
precepts.point: The covenant was made with Abraham, sworn to Isaac, and confirmed to Jacob as an everlasting covenant, giving Israel the land of Canaan as their inheritance.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 16: The Song Delivered into the Hand of Asaph

precepts.why:
This is the covenant “which he made with Abraham”: “I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.”

The Most High makes of Abraham a great nation, and in him all families of the earth are blessed. That covenant was sworn to Isaac and confirmed to Jacob “for a law, and to Israel for an everlasting covenant”, with the land of Canaan as Israel's inheritance.

precepts.text: Michal met David scornfully, David answered that he played before the Most High who chose him over Saul, and she had no child until her death.
precepts.point: Heman and Jeduthun with trumpets and instruments gave thanks because his mercy endureth forever, and all the people departed, and David returned to bless his house.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 16: The Song Delivered into the Hand of Asaph

precepts.why:
Chronicles ends with “David returned to bless his house.” Samuel shows what met him there: “Then David returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David”. She met him scornfully: “How glorious was the king of Israel to day, who uncovered himself to day in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself!”

David answered her, “It was before the Lord, which chose me before thy father, and before all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the Lord, over Israel: therefore will I play before the Lord. And I will yet be more vile than thus, and will be base in mine own sight”. He played before the Most High who chose him over Saul.

“Therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death.”

precepts.text: The bitter woman whose heart is snares and nets; the man who pleases the Most High escapes her.
precepts.point: Heman and Jeduthun with trumpets and instruments gave thanks because his mercy endureth forever, and all the people departed, and David returned to bless his house.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 16: The Song Delivered into the Hand of Asaph

precepts.why:
“And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.”

That is the bitter woman whose heart is snares and nets. When David returned to bless his house, Michal met him with scorn for playing before the Most High. But David had pleased the Most High, and the man who pleases the Most High escapes her.

points: The song calls all the earth to show forth his salvation and declare his glory among the heathen, for great is the Most High and greatly to be praised.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 16: The Song Delivered into the Hand of Asaph

points: All the gods of the people are idols, but the Most High made the heavens; strength and gladness are in his place, and all the earth is to fear before him.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 16: The Song Delivered into the Hand of Asaph

points: Let the heavens be glad, the earth rejoice, and the nations say the Most High reigns, for he cometh to judge the earth.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 16: The Song Delivered into the Hand of Asaph

points: The song ends with the plea to save, gather, and deliver Israel from the heathen, and all the people said Amen and praised the Most High. This is a good prayer to meditate on.
